ctx.x: He was good on bass drum or snare drum?

He was good on both, but he mostly played with snare drum. He was, uh, I thought it was short fella. His name was Joe, uh, Joe, uh, not Joe Watkins. Somebody else will probably tell us about him. Yeah, yeah, I can't think of that man's last, cause you want his right name.
Like Joe Watkins when we were talking to him, he came up with the fella that Bunk used to talk about two bits and then nobody knew his name. Do you remember two bits ever? No.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: So Joe Waskin asked me to go play.

ctx.x: It was Lawrence Murray's band, was it?

Yeah, it was Lawrence Murray. He couldn't go on to George Lewis' title because it was an organized band. But George, George Rosenthal told him, let's get him a good city. But he know most of the men's coming up there because he was down here. He came down here when we even was working at the paddock. Then we made another group. We come out the paddock, we made another group. When George, one time George Lewis split his band. Some of these men that won't go on the road like, such as Jim Crow and Kid Howard, with…
Well, uh, Bro. Well, uh, Bro.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: So, Si asked me, say, Joe, you want your job back?

ctx.x: And this Earl Watkins was playing the more modern stuff.

Yeah, he was playing the modern stuff. So naturally hired him, which didn't make me angry at all because I just had an idea I wasn't going to make it after the first two weeks with him. You know, I just didn't watch this. You're watching this is it. You just working on Back to the Army. Well, George was out there when I started playing with him. Yeah, Lawrence's cousin Si on drums then. Si Frazier?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: I see, just like, Saeed was out there last week at the hall. He was telling, say, you know, a lot of these fellas go around here and talk about they're playing the jazz beat, but they're not.

ctx.x: So I think there's a couple, a few years left, right? Huh? I think there's a few years left yet for the music.

I think there's quite a few years. Yeah, it's quite a few years. But I, now if, if they may call, call it jazz. You know, jazz is not a music of arrangements. You know, you don't play arrangements in jazz. Because that ain't the way it starts, that's not the authentic type. But you take a lot of these bands now, they call themselves jazz band, but they make an arrangement for the clarinet player, the trumpet player, or the trombone player, or the drummer, you know, man. No, no, I just hate sockets, I may have…
